title: Tray Bake: Mediterranean-Style Haloumi
subtitle: with Potato, Zucchini and Lemon
description: Whether you're full-time vego or part-time only, our varied range of vegetarian dishes really hits the spot. Bursting with veggies, dairy, legumes, grains and nuts, they're packed with flavour, they’ll fill you up and they're totally mouth-watering too!

steps.text: Parboil potatoes: Preheat the oven to 220C, fan-forced. Line an oven tray with baking paper. Cut the unpeeled potatoes into 3cm chunks. Put the potato in a medium saucepan of cold salted water and bring to the boil. Reduce the heat to medium and cook for 8 mins or until almost tender. Drain.

Prep ingredients: Meanwhile, crush or finely chop 1 garlic clove. Cut the zucchini into 2cm-thick rounds. Cut the tomatoes and onion into wedges. Finely grate the zest of half the lemon, then thinly slice the half. Juice the remaining lemon. Combine the garlic, lemon zest, lemon juice, Italian seasoning and 1½ tbs olive oil in a bowl. Season with salt and pepper.
Bake veggies: Put the potato, zucchini, tomato and onion on the lined tray. Drizzle with half the lemon mixture and toss to coat. Bake for 10 mins or until the veggies are almost tender.

Add haloumi: Slice the haloumi. Put the lemon slices and haloumi on top of the veggies and drizzle with the remaining lemon mixture. Bake for a further 15 mins or until the haloumi is golden and the potato is tender.
Serve up: Divide the veggies and haloumi among plates and enjoy!

Did you know?: Haloumi is a brined, slightly springy cheese originally from Cyprus. Traditionally it was made from a mixture of goat and sheep milk, although these days cow's milk is also used. The haloumi we use is made using vegetable rennet, so it's suitable for vegetarians.
